title: Maintaining Pool Water Chemistry
excerpt: Maintaining proper pool water chemistry is key to keeping your water clean, safe, and crystal clear. Here’s a simple breakdown of what to check and how to keep it balanced:
imageAlt: Long rectangular pool with wide pale paving and a covered cabana at the far end, under a blue sky with clouds.
seoTitle: Maintaining Pool Water Chemistry | Island Life Custom Pools
seoDescription: A simple breakdown of the pool water chemistry to check each week, the ideal ranges, and how to adjust chlorine, pH, alkalinity, calcium hardness, and stabilizer.

sections.title: 1. Chlorine (Sanitizer)
bullets: Ideal range: 1.0 – 3.0 ppm
Purpose: Kills bacteria, viruses, and algae
How to adjust: Use chlorine tablets, liquid chlorine, or granular chlorine

sections.title: 2. pH Level
bullets: Ideal range: 7.2 – 7.6
Purpose: Keeps water comfortable and prevents equipment damage
How to adjust: If pH is too low, add soda ash (sodium carbonate). If pH is too high, add muriatic acid or sodium bisulfate.

sections.title: 3. Total Alkalinity
bullets: Ideal range: 80 – 120 ppm
Purpose: Buffers pH, helps prevent rapid fluctuations
How to adjust: If it is too low, add baking soda (sodium bicarbonate). If it is too high, add acid (like for high pH), then aerate.

sections.title: 4. Calcium Hardness
bullets: Ideal range: 200 – 400 ppm
Purpose: Prevents corrosion (low) or scaling (high)
How to adjust: If it is too low, add calcium chloride. If it is too high, dilute the pool with fresh water.

sections.title: 5. Cyanuric Acid (Stabilizer)
bullets: Ideal range: 30 – 50 ppm (for outdoor pools)
Purpose: Protects chlorine from UV sunlight
How to adjust: If it is too low, add CYA (stabilizer). If it is too high, partially drain and refill the pool.

sections.title: 6. Phosphates & Metals (Optional)
bullets: Phosphates feed algae.
Use a phosphate remover if levels are high.

sections.title: Weekly Maintenance Checklist
bullets: Test water (use strips or a liquid test kit)
Adjust chemicals as needed
Skim, brush, and vacuum the pool
Clean skimmer baskets and filters
Shock the pool (especially after heavy use or rain)

sections.title: Quick Tips
bullets: Always add chemicals to water, never water to chemicals.
Wait at least 4–6 hours (or as directed) after adding chemicals before swimming.
Test your water at least twice a week, more often in hot weather or after a storm.
Keep a logbook or app to track chemical adjustments over time.
